request.initial_prompt: It was assumed, of course, that all this was done freely, and in good faith, by way of voluntary submission and salutary guidance. But, in fact, there was sometimes no little insincerity, and much that was false and strained in this practice. Yet the older and more experienced of the monks adhered to their opinion, arguing that "for those who have come within these walls sincerely seeking salvation, such obedience and sacrifice will certainly be salutary and of great benefit; those, on the other hand, who find it irksome, and repine, are no true monks, and have made a mistake in entering the monastery—their proper place is in the world. Even in the temple one cannot be safe from sin and the devil. So it was no good taking it too much into account."

It was assumed, of course, that all this was done freely, and in good faith, by way of
voluntary submission and salutary guidance.
But in fact, there was sometimes no little insincerity, and much that was false and strained
in this practice.
Yet the older and more experienced of the monks adhered to their opinion, arguing that,
for those who have come within these walls sincerely seeking salvation, such obedience
and sacrifice will certainly be salutary and of great benefit.
Those, on the other hand, who find it irksome and repine, are no true monks, and have made
a mistake in entering the monastery.
Their proper place is in the world.
Even in the temple one cannot be safe from sin and the devil.
So it was no good taking it too much into account.
